findings.finding: The 180-day post-closing lock-up (closing 2026-03-26) expired on the drop day, 2026-09-22. About 255M resale-registered shares became saleable against a prior float near 43M. Day-2 selling by early holders lands on 2026-09-23.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The lock-up ended on the drop day itself, so 2026-09-23 is the first full session after the first unlock day. By the 15:05 screen, turnover was about $174M, roughly 29-30M shares at about $5.9. Even if all of that were unlocked stock, it is about 11-12% of the ~255M newly saleable shares. The holders have cost bases far below spot: OMERS put in under US$30M across two rounds. So the supply is countable and mostly unspent, and it keeps arriving on the next session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last supply event on this name was the resale registration of ~294M shares on 2026-05-04 (-61.27%). The next close was -3.50% and the next open +0.29% (baseline history). The two positive rebounds in the history (2026-04-21 +51.75%, 2026-04-23 +7.28%) came while the float was about 43M, which a 6x larger float now dampens.
findings.why_not_priced: The gap priced the unlock EVENT, which was public, dated and flagged by the Globe on 09-20. It could not price the unlock FLOW: which of ~255M shares actually hit the tape on day two is unknown to the close. Almost all of the fall came at the open (gap share 0.96, intraday -0.93%). If the market had absorbed the supply, the price would show intraday exhaustion: a close well off the lows on falling volume. Instead the intraday leg is flat-to-down on 17x volume.

findings.finding: The $300M Yorkville standby equity purchase agreement (SEPA), a synthetic ATM, had about $232.8M of capacity left as of 2026-08-21. The issuer has drawn on it before (5.5M shares for $67.2M in Q2), and Yorkville's resale shares are registered, so a draw can be made on any session, including 2026-09-23.
findings.mechanism_in_window: An open, effective facility can be drawn on any trading day with no advance notice. The F-1 registering Yorkville's resale shares (30M) has been effective since 2026-06-01. Whatever Yorkville buys it sells into the market over the pricing period. Draws are not disclosed per event, so the only in-window channel is flow, not a headline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 draws averaged a net $12.28/share. The stock has since fallen about 55% with no separately identifiable draw-day reaction in the baseline. The facility's effect is diffuse drift, not a gap.
findings.why_not_priced: The close prices lock-up holders, not the issuer as a second seller competing for the same bids. Management says it draws 'only when we believe conditions are favorable', which argues against a draw at $5.8, so the size is kept small. If the market had fully priced a live issuer seller, no bid would show up on day two ahead of unlocked supply. That is unobservable here, hence the small size.
